newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran appeals for help to house its refugees.
newsitem.headline: Iran appeals for help to house its refugees.

text.p: Iran has told European envoys that tens of thousands of Kurdish refugees who fled Iraq to Iran faced bleak winter conditions at their mountainous camps and held the international community responsible for their plight.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Thursday that European ambassadors and diplomats based in Tehran had visited four refugee camps on Tuesday.

It said Kurdestan province governor Mohammad-Reza Rahimi told the envoys the international community "will be held responsible for any untoward incidents faced by Iraqi Kurdish refugees during the usually fierce winters of the region."

Rahimi "regretted the refugees have received virtually no other help from foreign countries except for the little aid provided by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)," IRNA added.
Iran is currently home to two million refugees, 1.4 million from Afghanistan and 600,000 from Iraq, making it the world's most important host country, according to the UNHCR.

On Wednesday Iran said 1,000 more Kurdish refugees had crossed into its territory on Tuesday, to join tens of thousands who had fled northern Iran since its takeover by a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction in September.

Iran, which said in late September it was sheltering 65,000 Kurdish refugees, has criticised international organisations, saying they were not providing enough help for the refugees living in tent camps in the cold mountainous border region.

Laurens Jolles, a UNHCR official, said on Wednesday there was a continued flow of refugees into Iran, although some were going back home. "There are some people going back (to Iraq), but definitely not as many as the number of people who are arriving," Jolles told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
"UNHCR is concerned about the situation of the refugees because of the proximity of the camps to the border and due to the climactic conditions," Jolles said.
UNHCR has urged Iran to move the camps away from the border.
